directAnswer: To check the current Git branch, use the command `git branch` in your terminal. The active branch will be highlighted with an asterisk.
summary: This guide provides steps to check your current Git branch across different platforms.

sections.heading: Checking Branch in Terminal
sections.body: You can check the current branch in Git using the terminal on any platform.

sections.heading: Checking Branch in GUI Tools
sections.body: If you are using a GUI tool like GitHub Desktop or SourceTree, the current branch is typically displayed in the interface, often at the top of the window.

steps.title: Open Terminal
steps.detail: Launch your terminal application (Command Prompt, PowerShell, Terminal, etc.) depending on your operating system.

steps.title: Navigate to Repository
steps.detail: Use the `cd` command to navigate to your Git repository directory.

steps.title: Run Git Command
steps.detail: Type `git branch` and press Enter. The current branch will be marked with an asterisk.

faqs.question: What if I don't see any branches listed?
faqs.answer: If no branches are listed, ensure you are inside a valid Git repository. You can initialize one using `git init`.

faqs.question: Can I check branches in a remote repository?
faqs.answer: Yes, use `git branch -r` to list remote branches.

faqs.question: How do I switch branches?
faqs.answer: Use the command `git checkout branch-name` to switch to a different branch.

caveats: Ensure you have Git installed and configured on your system.
Commands may vary slightly based on your Git version.
